content: The implementation of sustainable Voluntary Medical Male Circumcision (VMMC) services necessitates the establishment of a robust logistics system. This system must encompass the procurement of medical commodities, effective supply chain management, adequate human resources, proper waste management, and appropriate storage solutions, including the safe storage of medical waste. Key Components and Considerations: Norms, Standards, and Policies: Nationally established standards must ensure the quality of VMMC supplies and guarantee uninterrupted procurement processes. Standardized guidelines and implementation strategies should promote the rational use of VMMC supplies and equipment. Procurement and Distribution: National procurement systems must be in place for VMMC supplies and equipment. A national supply and distribution system should ensure the availability of VMMC supplies and equipment. Quality: The quality of VMMC equipment and supplies, including male circumcision devices, must be maintained. Waste management systems should address the segregation, storage, transportation, treatment, and disposal of all relevant healthcare waste categories. Leadership and Governance: Ministries and higher levels of government must provide effective leadership to foster sustainable, adolescent-responsive policies and programs. This includes areas such as finance, youth engagement, and education. VMMC should be integrated into the Essential Package of Health Services and included in the national health strategy and operational plans. Task distribution plans, including task shifting and task sharing, should be developed and implemented. Service Delivery: High-quality health services must deliver effective, safe, and reliable health interventions to those in need, at the right time and place, within an integrated, people-centered framework. VMMC services should be institutionalized as part of the routine health system service delivery structure. Access: Comprehensive assessments of VMMC service delivery should be conducted, focusing on inclusivity. Mapping of existing service delivery infrastructure and resources is essential to inform planning and implementation in both community-based and health facility settings. Demand creation activities should be tailored to the specific context and target audience. Adverse event reporting systems must align with national frameworks. Critical Enablers: Adolescent and youth leadership and participation are crucial. Community engagement is essential for success. Multisectoral partnerships should be established to enhance program effectiveness. Enabling laws and policies must be in place to support VMMC services. Transitioning to Sustainability: The WHO framework for sustainability is built on six health system building blocks. These include leadership and governance, service delivery, health workforce, information systems, access to essential medicines, and financing. Countries must take a leading role in mobilizing, allocating, and managing resources effectively. Support and supervision should be person-centered, focusing on adolescent-friendly, integrated services. Collaboration with community organizations and networks can improve access for adolescents. Discussion Questions: 1. What has been the most challenging health system building block in your country, and why? What steps are needed to address this challenge? 2. What are your key requests or needs to advance VMMC implementation? 3. Would additional technical resources or tools assist you in implementing VMMC services effectively? If so, please specify. Closing: The WHO guidelines on preventing HIV through safe, voluntary medical male circumcision for adolescent boys and men in generalized HIV epidemics provide a comprehensive framework for action. Thank you for your participation in this TeleECHO series.
